phase: Phase 9 ML Baseline & Historical Model Audit

model_v1_baseline.vulnerability: Severe cross-split duplicate leakage; unconstrained sliding window.

model_v2_historical.vulnerability: Sliding window (300) missed distant duplicate pairs. 94% FPR on unseen dry pavement.

model_v3_clean.vulnerability: 5 cross-split near-duplicate leak pairs; complete source-label confounding.

model_v3_monsoon.vulnerability: Source-label confounding (Clemson floods vs Virenbr11 potholes). Metadata baseline reaches 83.78%.

verified_historical_findings: Random image splitting causes severe duplicate leakage when multi-frame camera bursts are unclustered.
Exact MD5 deduplication is insufficient: perceptual near-duplicates (dhash Hamming distance <= 2) must be grouped.
Sliding-window clustering is fundamentally flawed: near-duplicates separated by > window size escape into opposing splits.
Global exhaustive N x N pairwise Hamming comparison successfully unifies all historical leak pairs.
Balancing classes across distinct datasets (Clemson floods vs Virenbr11 roads) does NOT solve source confounding.
Non-semantic metadata features (width, height, file size) achieve 85.97% test accuracy on Manifest V4, proving active shortcut learning potential.
Production Vision V4 training must remain locked in NO-GO status until multi-class paired road imagery is collected.
baseline_conclusion: The baseline repository is in an auditable, high-integrity state. All previous model checkpoints are preserved. Data leakage is cured in Manifest V4, but source-label confounding remains 100% active. Phase 9 must execute diagnostic and transfer tracks without training an unvalidated production checkpoint.
